extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, researchers, and editors tracking political disinformation and fake-news websites
extracted.subtask_description: Create or use a country-organized list of websites and domains identified by journalists, researchers, and platform enforcement as distributing false news, participating in disinformation campaigns, or being linked to political actors or influence operations. The list records domain, status, notes (why flagged), and sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criterion — judged by journalists and researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Websites included are those that "have both been considered by journalists and researchers as distributing false news - or otherwise participating in disinformation - and have been designated by journalists and researchers as likely being linked to political actors."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the article's primary standard for listing a site: independent coverage/analysis by journalists and academic/research groups identifying the site as distributing false news or participating in disinformation and linking it to political actors. Entries should cite reliable sources showing those judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linked to marketing/public relations firms
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites or networks that are "linked to... a marketing/public relations firm" (e.g., Ayam Agency) and are part of a coordinated content/asset ecosystem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when investigative work or platform takedowns identify corporate/service providers (PR firms, marketing agencies) that create or support networks of domains and social accounts to amplify narratives. Example notes cite the firm and explain the relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related to networks removed for "coordinated inauthentic behavior"
rubrics_metrics.description: Domains that are "related to a network of Facebook pages and accounts removed... for coordinated inauthentic behavior."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flagged when platform enforcement reports (Facebook/Twitter removals) or analyses explicitly link domains to removed coordinated inauthentic operations. Notes typically reference the platform report or takedown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part of multi-year cross-platform influence campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites described in research as elements of a "multi-year cross-platform effort to advance the interests" of a political leader or actor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when longitudinal research (e.g., Graphika) documents sustained, cross-platform campaigns and places domains within that operation; entry should summarize the campaign goal as reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spreads specific misleading/false narratives (content-based indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites that "spread climate change denialism", "anti-vaccine misinformation", false claims about events or government actions, genocide denial, unproven COVID-19 cures, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content-based reason for listing: summarise the misleading narratives the site is documented to push and cite fact-checks or research identifying those narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owned by or operated by political operatives / campaign staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Domains "owned by" or run by individuals linked to political campaigns or politicians (e.g., digital communications chief of a political figure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when ownership or staffing links to political actors are documented in reliable sources; include the named owner/operator and their political affiliations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linked to a political party or politician
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites "linked to the Freedom Party of Austria", or other parties/politicians, indicating partisan or actor-aligned operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when reporting shows organizational, editorial, or funding ties to a party or named political actor. Note the party/actor and the source that establishes the link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accused by government authorities or enforcement bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Domains "accused by the United States Department of the Treasury" (or similar) of close links to a named political actor or illicit activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority-based indicator: include quotations/summaries from the accusing body and link to the official statement or report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposter/spoof sites and typosquatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites that are "imposter news portal" or "Spoof of [legitimate outlet]" (typosquatting or imitation of reputable news organizations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag cases where a domain intentionally mimics a real outlet's name/branding; include the legitimate outlet being spoofed and any evidence (e.g., copied logos, near-identical names).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of IDN homograph attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Domains using internationalized domain name (IDN) homograph tricks (e.g., replacing the Latin 'i' with Turkish 'ı') to masquerade as legitimate outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document specific homograph or character-substitution examples and cite technical analyses explaining the spoof technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ephemeral disinformation techniques (delete-after-engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactics described as "ephemeral disinformation": articles are deleted after receiving engagement and URLs are linked to the site they falsely portray.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when researchers (e.g., Citizen Lab) document intentional deletion/ephemerality as a technique to amplify then hide content; summarize the behaviour and example(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content duplication across multiple domains/networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites that "published the same content as" other domains or are copies of each other (content duplication across networked sites).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates coordinated reuse of content to amplify reach; note the domains that share identical content and the source documenting the duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymously registered or obfuscated domain registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries noting "anonymously registered website" or "missing domain registration name" as a sign of concealment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational red flag: include registrar/WHOIS details if cited by sources and explain how registration obscurity factors into the assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linked to state-sponsored or government-backed campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Domains identified as part of "state-sponsored disinformation" or "active measures" attributed to a government (e.g., Russia, Iran).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when attribution to a state actor is reported by reputable research organizations or governments; capture the attribution source and summary of the state's alleged goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linked to pseudonymous operators suspected of sponsorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites connected to pseudonymous individuals "suspected of being sponsored by" a government or external advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include investigative findings that point to pseudonymous operators and the nature of suspected sponsorship (financial, strategic, etc.). Cite the investigative report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linked to commercial digital-marketing infrastructure/firms
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites tied to digital marketing firms (e.g., Bee Interactive, DotDev, NewWaves) that provide infrastructure for influence campaigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the firm named by investigators and the role (hosting, content production, social amplification) attributed to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of platform manipulation techniques (purchased likes/engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices such as "purchasing social media interactions (likes)" or other manipulation of social metrics to simulate popularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag when academic or platform reports document paid interaction purchasing or other manipulation; include legal or platform-policy notes where mentioned (e.g., possible violation of marketing practices act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of programmatic advertising / ad monetization channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that domains placed advertisements programmatically (e.g., Google ads) to monetize content, sometimes removed after reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include findings from ad-tech investigations (e.g., ProPublica) showing ad placements tied to flagged domains and any subsequent removals or advertiser responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harassment, malware or other harmful operational behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites accused of "harassing journalists", containing scripts used for cryptocurrency mining, or other malicious behaviors beyond misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record reported malicious technical behaviors or harassment campaigns tied to a domain, citing the investigative source or platform enforcement action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation with ideological or extremist groups / military actors
rubrics_metrics.description: Domains "affiliated with" specific ideological groups or part of influence operations involving military or extremist actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document affiliation claims and provide citation; used when ideological alignment is a primary reason for flagging and when it influences the site's content and targeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operations described as content farms / 'pink-slime' pseudo-news or pay-to-play local networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites operating as content farms, 'pink-slime' pseudo-news outlets, pay-to-play local news networks, or 'zombie content farms' producing churned content for influence or profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when reporting characterizes a network's business model (content-farm churn, paid local-news networks) and links it to political influence or monetization strategies; cite the exposé or research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of fabricated quotes or false attributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites that contain fabricated quotes or fabricated attributions (e.g., invented quotes suggesting intelligence service involvement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag examples where investigators identify fabricated quotes or documents and include the specific allegation and source analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impersonation of official government websites
rubrics_metrics.description: Domains spoofing government sites (e.g., "bundesergierung.de" spoofing the Bundesregierung) to mislead readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the official site being impersonated and provide the investigative source explaining how the domain was used to mislead.
